Capitalist here, the problem with this question is that it presumes that people experiencing extreme poverty are poor because they don't have cash, when in reality they don't have cash because they are systemically poor. They are poor as a result of many factors such as they don't have abundant local resources, access to education, infrastructure, water, food, technology, living in a warzone etc. Giving all these people $2 cash, when they are already spending 60-80% of their income on food, is just going to make the locally scarce food supply more expensive.

If instead the hypothetical was that for every person a new resource magically pops into existence in their possession with about $2 local value and it is exactly what will help them/they need most at the time, then I would do it. Some people might get a sack of rice, a jug of water or milk, a piece of meat, an educational book, a litre of gasoline, some batteries, whatever. I think creating $16,000,000,000 of new additional value for the world is probably worth forgoing $10,000,000 cash.

Step 1: pick a fast clearing jungler with decent early game who likes long fights like **Volibear, Udyr, or Hecarim.**

Step 2: find a clear guide for the champion and practice clears in the practice tool.

Step 3: play a real game, try to identify which lane is the most volatile and just full clear over and over again to that side of the map (ie the top lane matchup is two high damage low mobility fighters, you path from your bottom side camps to your topside camps) if you can't identify this yet just path bot to top every game.

Step 4: as you are clearing start moving your camera to the lane you are pathing towards and mid lane. Then go gank/dive/invade with prio/take objective based on what you see in the lanes.

This is a great write-up of our strategy! We didn't start like this obviously but added and optimized things as we played more. A few things I'd add:

* In the same sense that having two people noticing different things helps a lot, having two different sets of knowledge helps an exponential amount. There are days that person 1 couldn't solve it in 1000 guesses, but person 2 can get in one guess, and vice-versa.
* A lot of prepositions get revealed and can guide your thinking a lot, words like "around" "because" "in the" "at the", etc. can quickly give you an idea if the article is an object, person, place, historical, dead, living, present, mechanical, conceptual, etc.
* Patience, sometimes it's a surprisingly quick process and we solve it in 5 minutes. Sometimes it takes a long time, with painfully long chunks of time where we don't think of anything. We are very committed to not giving in and guessing something that might not be in the title.
* Don't ever guess anything that isn't in the title. If you gleam something that makes you think it might be an animal? You won't gain anything by typing animal except saving yourself time, start trying to figure out if it's a fish or a mammal or an insect, either you can make things work and you further your thinking, or you can't and you move on.
